text:
tara-support: Hey team — escalation from AcmeCorp: users can view projects after SSO login but get 403 when trying to create resources (API + console). Ticket #12345. Can someone help triage?

customer-alex: seeing this too. Steps: login via Okta, switch org -> open project -> click 'Create dataset' -> 403. Works if I sign out and use API key.

mike-sre: thanks. Do we have a repro curl + response body? Also need the SSO assertion (claims) and token scopes.

tara-support: repro curl pasted below (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/px123/datasets -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name":"test-ds"}'
```
Response: `{"error":"permission_denied","message":"403: insufficient permissions"}`

tara-support: customer also attached id_token and access_token JWTs (okta env). I pulled the access_token scopes: `openid profile email` (no custom project scopes).

ashley-idp: @tara-support can you paste the SAML/OIDC claim dump for the user? We usually map `redwood_roles` or `groups` to project roles. If scopes are minimal maybe role claim didn't come through.

customer-alex: pasted in support UI. Claim `roles: ["viewer"]` in id_token but our console shows them as `editor` in the org UI earlier today. Strange.

mike-sre: That mismatch smells like stale session state: console caches role bindings for the session but token claim is authoritative for API calls. If the token says viewer you'll get 403 for write. Did the customer recently change role in IdP?

tara-support: They said they were promoted from viewer->editor this morning via SCIM. Promotion appears in org UI immediately. But API calls still get 403.

eng-infra-javier: Deploy bot log shows a rollout to auth-proxy at 2026-03-12T03:10Z (last night). @deploy-bot can you confirm?

deploy-bot: auth-proxy v2.14.1 rolled at 2026-03-12T03:12Z to prod region-us-east-1 :white_check_mark:

eng-infra-javier: OK — possible token/session cache invalidation bug after proxy change. Two hypotheses: (1) SCIM change updates our backend but existing sessions keep old group claim until re-auth, (2) our session cache isn't invalidating when SCIM sets role mapping and we favor cached RBAC.

mike-sre: Quick repro for us: 1) provision user as viewer in IdP, 2) sign in, confirm view-only, 3) change IdP role to editor via SCIM, 4) without signing out, attempt write -> does it 403? If yes, that's session-refresh problem.

tara-support: Customer confirmed they did exactly that and didn't sign out. Workaround they found: sign out and sign in again -> write works.

ashley-idp: That matches: SCIM updated membership but Okta did not push a back-channel session refresh to the browser. We rely on token lifetime + refresh. If the access_token didn't get refreshed, API sees old claims.

eng-infra-javier: For hosted customers: we should invalidate server-side session cache when we receive SCIM role-change webhooks. Do we currently do that?

mike-sre: I thought SCIM webhook only triggers a background sync, not immediate session invalidation. Need to check code path. @eng-infra-javier can you triage whether webhook handler calls session.invalidate(user_id)?

eng-infra-javier: I'll look now. If not, short-term we can document that role changes require re-login or a forced token refresh. Long-term: add session invalidation on SCIM change + add a per-user `last_role_change_at` check in auth-proxy so tokens issued before that are treated as stale.

tara-support: Customer asks for a mitigation we can apply for their org right now. Any admin-side options?

mike-sre: Admin can force revoke sessions via Console -> Org Settings -> Active sessions -> Revoke all. That will force users to re-auth. Tell customer to do that as immediate fix.

customer-alex: did that and re-logged in — create succeeded. Thanks.

ashley-idp: We'll also check Okta event hooks; if Okta supports a user.session.end event on SCIM update that we can subscribe to, we can automate.

eng-infra-javier: Action items: 1) ENG-INFRA - confirm webhook handler does NOT invalidate sessions (P0) 2) ENG-INFRA - add `last_role_change_at` token check in auth-proxy (P1) 3) DEVEX - update support KB: "Role changes require re-auth / admin revoke sessions" (P2) 4) Support follow up to confirm customer revoking sessions fixed issue.

mike-sre: I'll own triage and assign a ticket in JIRA to ENG-INFRA with logs and deploy timestamp.

tara-support: Closing loop with customer now. I'll mark incident as escalated -> eng-infra. Thanks all :thumbsup:

customer-alex: appreciate the fast help!
